introduction: “O peoples of the earth!” Bahá’u’lláh begins a great many passages with these words, written from exile and from the prison of ‘Akká and addressed to no one nation or church. The call is nearly always the same: the One promised in every scripture has come; look with fairness; hear; do not hesitate; let go of what you hold. A hundred of the guide’s 191 quotations are given here, ten from each tenth of its length, and because they repeat one another on purpose they are best read slowly. Beside them stand a hundred voices from elsewhere, almost all of them earlier calls of the same kind: the prophets’ “Hear, O earth”, Wisdom crying at the gates, “Come unto me”, the Qur’an’s “O mankind!”, with the rules for a fair hearing that Proverbs, Nicodemus and the Bereans supply. About one in seven raises the hearer’s side of the matter and ends in a question: the warnings against false prophets and false Christs, the test in Deuteronomy, Mill on hearing the other side, Paul on the powers that be.
questions: “Be fair, O people!” Proverbs, Nicodemus and the Bereans each say what a fair hearing is. What would it mean, in practice, to give a religious claim one?
The readings say the One promised in all the scriptures has come. Jesus and Deuteronomy warn against false claimants. How should a careful person hold both the openness and the caution?
The call comes from a prison and claims “manifest sovereignty”. Zechariah’s king rides a donkey. What kind of authority is being asserted, and how is it recognized?
“Cast away what ye possess.” What, in your own case, would have to be put down in order to listen, and what should be kept?
Most people, say these passages, remain heedless and asleep; Jesus compares his own generation to the days of Noah. What is it about ordinary life that makes such calls hard to hear?
The same few sentences are repeated across dozens of tablets. What does repetition do to a reader, and why might a call to the whole world take this form?

outside.why: “Cast away … the things ye possess, and immerse yourselves in this Ocean” where pearls lie hidden. Jesus’ man who finds treasure in a field: for joy thereof he goeth and selleth all that he hath.
“Adorn your temples with the ornament of tranquility and dignity.” Peter: the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.
“Strife, dispute and conflict have been forbidden … This is the Day of reformation.” Isaiah: neither shall they learn war any more.
“Look with the eye of fairness at that which hath been sent down.” Isaiah’s God asks for a hearing in the same spirit: come now, and let us reason together.
“Judge fairly concerning that which has been revealed.” Proverbs: he that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
“Be fair, O people! If ye deny Him, by what path will ye approach?” Jesus told his followers to expect false claimants and believe them not. What would a fair examination of such a claim consist of?
“He Who was promised in the Books of God hath come … to reform the world.” Haggai: the desire of all nations shall come.
“We ask of you no recompense in this Cause.” The Qur’an gives this as a mark of the true messenger: follow those who ask of you no fee.
The Wronged One “calleth out from the Most Great Prison unto all nations”. Paul in chains: the word of God is not bound.
“O people of the world!” The Psalm addresses the same audience: give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world, both low and high, rich and poor, together.
“To Me, to Me, O peoples of earth and heaven!” Jesus: come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
“His Cause is more manifest than the sun.” The Qur’an to all mankind: now hath a proof from your Lord come unto you, and We have sent down unto you a clear light.
“Come ye, that I may recount unto you the Most Great News.” Isaiah’s herald: lift up thy voice with strength; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God!
“Come ye, come ye, that I may cause you to hear the call of God.” Wisdom in Proverbs stands in the high places and cries at the gates: unto you, O men, I call.
“He Who was promised throughout the ages and centuries hath come.” Simeon, who had waited his whole life: mine eyes have seen thy salvation.
“The gate of divine generosity hath been opened.” Revelation: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it.
“The Most Great Gate hath been opened.” The Psalm: lift up your heads, O ye gates; and the King of glory shall come in.
“Awake, awake, for, lo! the Gate of God is open.” Paul quotes an early hymn: awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead.
“It is incumbent upon the peoples of both the East and the West to obey My word.” Muḥammad was told to say: O mankind! I am the messenger of God to you all.
The Báb claims the allegiance of East and West. Peter claimed as much for another name. When two such claims meet, what do the readings ask of the hearer?
“We have summoned the whole world.” The first words of Jesus’ preaching in Mark: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand.
“He Who was promised in the Psalms and Tablets has come.” The risen Christ on the road: beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them the things concerning himself.
“That which was promised in the Scriptures of God hath appeared.” Moses’ promise of a prophet to come.
“He Whom the Messengers of God have heralded hath appeared.” Malachi: the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple.
“The Day is come, but the people are in manifest darkness.” Isaiah: the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
“He Who was promised in the Books of God and concealed from His servants has come.” Jesus’ promise of another Comforter.
“The appointed time is fulfilled.” Paul: when the fulness of the time was come.
“The Day hath come wherein God hath fulfilled His promise.” Jesus at Nazareth: this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
“What was treasured in the Books of God … has been made manifest.” Moses: the secret things belong unto the Lord, but those things which are revealed belong unto us.
“Cast away what ye possess and take hold of that which hath been sent down.” Paul: what things were gain to me, those I counted loss.
“Every sect was promised the meeting with God … yet when He appeared in truth they disbelieved.” John: he came unto his own, and his own received him not.

Each community was promised, and each refused. Deuteronomy shows why a community might be careful: how shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? Is caution towards a new claim always disbelief?
“Every wearer of a white turban lamented”: the divines seized on fancies. Jesus to the scribes: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men.
“This is the Day whose mention was sent down in the Qur’an.” The verse.
“He is verily the One Who spoke on Sinai.” The first time: God called unto him out of the midst of the bush.
The Divine Lote-Tree proclaims: “Verily, I am God.” The Qur’an’s account of the voice Moses heard.
“The Fire of the Tree is blazing and speaking forth.” Israel at Sinai heard the voice out of the fire and begged not to hear it again, lest they die. Why would people ask for a go-between?
“There is none other God but Me, the Peerless.” The oldest form of the proclamation: Hear, O Israel.
“Those who lay in their graves have arisen.” Ezekiel: behold, O my people, I will open your graves.
The Mount declared that those in the graves have arisen. Jesus: the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God.
“The Hour hath called out, and the Resurrection proclaimeth.” The Qur’an: the hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain.
The Hour and the Resurrection are announced as present events. Paul staked his preaching on a bodily rising in history. What does “the Hour has come” ask a traditional believer to reconsider?
“The gates of heaven have been opened, the clouds pour down their rain.” Malachi: prove me now, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.
“Rejoice, for the veil hath been rent asunder.” Matthew at the crucifixion: the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

“The Cock of the Throne has crowed … O heedless ones!” FitzGerald’s Khayyám opens with a waking cry too, and what he wakes his reader to is wine and the shortness of life. What does each voice want the sleeper to wake to?
“The rapture of divine revelation hath taken hold of all created things.” The Psalm: let the field be joyful; then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice before the Lord: for he cometh.
“The Suns of eternity have shone forth.” Isaiah: the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together.
“The Herald hath called out: ‘The Kingdom belongeth unto God.’” The heralds over Bethlehem: glory to God in the highest.
“He for Whose manifestation and advent the worlds were created hath come.” Paul of Christ: all things were created by him, and for him.
“All things have proclaimed: ‘The Sovereign hath come!’” Jesus, asked to silence his disciples: the stones would immediately cry out.
“The Lord of heaven hath come with manifest sovereignty.” Zechariah’s king comes lowly, riding upon an ass. What kind of sovereignty is claimed by one who speaks from a prison?

The peaks are lit “while ye remain among the heedless”. Jesus: as it was in the days of Noe, they did eat, they drank, they married, until the flood came. Why does the ordinary business of life so reliably drown out a call like this?
“He Who was hidden from all eyes and concealed in all hearts has appeared.” Moses asked to see and was shown only what a man can bear.
“This is the Day wherein what was hidden in the Treasury of God … hath been revealed.” Jesus: many prophets have desired to see those things which ye see.
“This is the Day of Bounty.” The Psalm: this is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
“Remember the favor of God.” The Psalm: bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
The Ancient Lord “bringeth you glad tidings”. The angel to the shepherds: I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
“Cast away what the people possess and take what ye are bidden by God.” Jesus to a rich young man: sell that thou hast, and come and follow me.
“The Promise hath come.” Habakkuk had written for those still waiting: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come.
“Hearken unto My call and be not of the heedless ones.” Hebrews: to day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
“Know ye the worth of these days.” Jesus, weeping over Jerusalem: thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
“Turn ye toward Him with your hearts.” Isaiah: look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth.
He commands “righteousness and God-consciousness”. The Preacher’s conclusion: fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
“O dwellers of earth! Hearken unto the call of your Lord.” Jeremiah: O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord.
“Raise up your heads from the couch of heedlessness.” Paul: now it is high time to awake out of sleep.
“The Day of Hearing has come.” Jesus’ refrain: he that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
“Blessed is the ear that hath attained.” The Qur’an: a reminder for him who hath a heart, or giveth ear with full intelligence.
“He hath appeared Who summoneth all unto God.” The Qur’an: O mankind! The messenger hath come unto you with the Truth from your Lord.
He summons the peoples and announces what is ordained. Ezekiel’s commission: whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear, they shall know that there hath been a prophet among them.
“There is none other God but I.” The first words from Sinai.
“Verily, there is none other God but Me.” The Qur’an: God is witness that there is no God save Him.

“The Day of the Promise is come.” The Qur’an records the question unbelievers have always asked: when will this promise be fulfilled, if ye are truthful? What kind of evidence do those who ask it expect?
“He hath manifested Me with clear proof and sent Me.” Jesus to the woman at the well: I that speak unto thee am he.
“The Lord of Names hath come, riding upon the clouds.” Revelation: behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him.

He has come on the clouds, says the tablet, and from a prison. Daniel saw one like the Son of man come with the clouds of heaven. What did the first hearers of that image expect to see, and what do the readings ask them to see instead?
“The banners of guidance have been raised upon every lofty and exalted mountain.” Isaiah: the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains.
“Be not of the heedless ones.” The Qur’an: their reckoning draweth nigh for mankind, while they turn away in heedlessness.
“Turn ye unto Him, and be not of the heedless.” Jeremiah’s God: I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not.
“Follow not your desires. Follow Him Who hath come.” Jesus: laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men.

“Follow not every ignorant remote one.” Jesus: beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing. Each side of every religious dispute has used that verse of the other; what would settle it?
“Draw nigh and be not of them that hesitate.” Elijah on Carmel: how long halt ye between two opinions?
“Be fair in the Cause of God.” Nicodemus to the council: doth our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he doeth?

“Be fair in your judgment regarding this Light.” The people of Berea are praised for it: they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

“Cast away what ye possess of idle fancies. The Sun of Certitude hath dawned.” Plato’s prisoner has to be dragged up into the light and is at first blinded by it. Why is giving up a fancy so painful, even for the truth?
“Follow not every remote clamourer.” The first Psalm: blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly.
People are told not to follow those who have denied the Proof. Mill: he who knows only his own side of the case knows little of that. Does fairness require hearing the deniers out?
“Follow not those whom the world hath deluded with its vanities.” John: love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
The world and its ornaments “shall pass away and are accounted … but numbered days”. James: what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time.
“How long will ye slumber upon the couch of heedlessness?” Proverbs: how long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard?
“The Call hath been raised in truth, yet most of the people remain asleep.” Paul: let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch.
“Know your stations and follow not every ignorant remote one.” The Qur’an: be not as those who say, we hear, and they hear not.

“Lay aside the books of the populace and take hold of the Book of God.” Milton: as good almost kill a man as kill a good book. What is to be laid aside, and what kept, of all that people have written?
“Abandon the books of idle fancies and vain imaginings.” The Preacher: of making many books there is no end.
“Beware lest ye hesitate. Hasten unto Him.” The fishermen of Galilee: they straightway left their nets.
“This is not a day for tarrying.” Isaiah: seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near.
“Reject not the truth with your mouths. Answer Him.” James: be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.
“Beware lest the conditions of creation withhold you.” The invited guests of the parable: they all with one consent began to make excuse.
“Cast behind you every command and then follow Him Who speaks with truth.” Peter: we ought to obey God rather than men.
Every other command is to be put behind. Paul: let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. How have believers decided which commands may be set aside?
“The Promised One hath come, calling all unto God.” Isaiah was warned at his own calling how such a call is received: hear ye indeed, but understand not.

jeremiah-o-earth-earth-earth.text: O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the Lord

psalm-hear-this-all-ye-people.text: Hear this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world: Both low and high, rich and poor, together

matthew-come-unto-me.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light

mark-kingdom-is-at-hand.text: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel

hebrews-today-if-ye-will-hear.text: While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation

proverbs-answereth-before-he-heareth.text: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him

acts-bereans.text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so

ezekiel-hear-or-forbear.text: For they are impudent children and stiffhearted. I do send thee unto them; and thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God. And they, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear, (for they are a rebellious house,) yet shall know that there hath been a prophet among them

isaiah-spread-out-my-hands.text: I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts

jeremiah-rising-up-early.text: And now, because ye have done all these works, saith the Lord, and I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not

peter-meek-and-quiet-spirit.text: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price

psalm-lift-up-your-heads.text: Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle

revelation-open-door.text: I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name

luke-beginning-at-moses.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself

deuteronomy-voice-out-of-the-fire.text: And ye said, Behold, the Lord our God hath shewed us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire: we have seen this day that God doth talk with man, and he liveth. Now therefore why should we die? for this great fire will consume us: if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, then we shall die. For who is there of all flesh, that hath heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived

ezekiel-open-your-graves.text: Therefore prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves

matthew-veil-of-the-temple.text: Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost. And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent

psalm-let-the-heavens-rejoice.text: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof. Let the field be joyful, and all that is therein: then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice Before the Lord: for he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness, and the people with his truth

isaiah-all-flesh-shall-see-it.text: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it

isaiah-behold-your-god.text: O Zion, that bringest good tidings, get thee up into the high mountain; O Jerusalem, that bringest good tidings, lift up thy voice with strength; lift it up, be not afraid; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God

psalm-forget-not-all-his-benefits.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits

matthew-ears-to-hear.text: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear

isaiah-look-unto-me.text: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else

matthew-sheeps-clothing.text: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves

james-life-is-a-vapour.text: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away

isaiah-seek-ye-the-lord.text: Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon

proverbs-riches-profit-not.text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death

quran-messenger-to-you-all.text: Say (O Muhammad): O mankind! Lo! I am the messenger of Allah to you all - (the messenger of) Him unto Whom belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. There is no Allah save Him. He quickeneth and He giveth death. So believe in Allah and His messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write, who believeth in Allah and in His Words, and follow him that haply ye may be led aright.

quran-messenger-hath-come-with-truth.text: O mankind! The messenger hath come unto you with the Truth from your Lord. Therefor believe; (it is) better for you. But if ye disbelieve, still, lo! unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth. Allah is ever Knower, Wise.

quran-proof-from-your-lord.text: O mankind! Now hath a proof from your Lord come unto you, and We have sent down unto you a clear light;

quran-mankind-stand-before-the-lord.text: The day when (all) mankind stand before the Lord of the Worlds?

quran-who-ask-of-you-no-fee.text: Follow those who ask of you no fee, and who are rightly guided.

quran-who-hath-a-heart.text: Lo! therein verily is a reminder for him who hath a heart, or giveth ear with full intelligence.

quran-we-hear-and-they-hear-not.text: Be not as those who say, we hear, and they hear not.
